newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mobutu, ready to return home, urges Zaire truce.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu, ready to return home, urges Zaire truce.

text.p: Ailing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko called on Thursday for a ceasefire in his strife-torn country and the creation of a national council to find a solution to the crisis.

His appeal was issued on the eve of his scheduled return home to Kinshasa. A spokesman said the Zairean leader would leave Nice airport at 8 a.m. (0700 GMT) on Friday and arrive in his capital the same day at 3 p.m. (1400 GMT).

"At a time when I am preparing to return to my country to find myself again among my people, I invite all Zaireans to rise together," he said in a written statement sent to news agencies in Paris from his villa on the French Riviera.
Mobutu said he welcomed all regional and international efforts to bring peace to Zaire.
"I call on those who hold any responsibilities and who love their country to gather together to resolve the crisis.
"There must be a ceasefire to put an end to the sufferings which our people are enduring and to allow humanitarian aid to be sent in safe conditions to those who need it," he said.

Mobutu called for creation of a national council "including the various currents (of opinion) and sensitivities, the army and parliament which must be rapidly set up to find, together with our brothers - with no exclusions - the appropriate ways to emerge from the situation so direly affecting our dear country."
Mobutu said a campaign to organise new elections should begin without delay "to designate representatives freely chosen by the people."
Mobutu's statement was issued a day after he left hospital where he had treatment following an operation for prostate cancer last August. He spent most of his time in Europe since.

His son and spokesman, Nzanga, has said his father did not rule out talks with rebels led by Laurent Kabila who have been pressing deeper into Zaire from the east but that had to be done in agreement with the government and parliament.
The rebels insist only face-to-face talks between Kabila and Mobutu can halt the fighting.
France meanwhile advised its nationals to leave Zaire and sent troops and aircraft to nearby Congo and Gabon to protect them if need be.

Zaire's main opposition group, the Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS) of veteran radical Etienne Tshisekedi, said it shared Kabila's aim of toppling Mobutu and had sent envoys to talk to him.
Prime Minister Kenga wa Dondo, under fire for his handling of the war, returned home on Thursday from Kenya, where he backed a regional call for a truce and talks.
While he was away, the transitional parliament voted to sack him in a vote rejected by his and Mobutu supporters as invalid.
